# Positive periods (`positive_period_pct`)

*Category: Consistency · Nature: observed · Unit: fraction · Formula id: `positive_period_pct@v1` · Methodology 0.1.0*

## 1. What does it measure?

Share of periods with a strictly positive return (hit rate).

## 2. Formula

```text
#{t : r_t > 0} / n
```

## 3. Required inputs

Periodic simple returns.

## 4. Is higher or lower better?

Higher is better.

## 5. Plain-language interpretation

How often the investment made money in a period.

## 6. Professional interpretation

Win rate on the supplied frequency; says nothing about the size of wins and losses (see gain-to-pain, Omega). A very high hit rate with small gains can mask rare large losses.

## 7. Assumptions

- Zero returns count as neither positive nor negative.

## 8. When can it be misleading?

- Returns are smoothed or stale, which inflates the share of small positive periods.

## 9. Minimum sensible data

One observation; low confidence below 3 years. (policy `location`: Mean-type estimates: low confidence below 3 years, moderate below 5 years.)

## 10. Reference implementations

| Library | Function | Agrees | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| QuantStats 0.0.81 | `stats.win_rate` | no (documented difference) | QuantStats excludes zero-return periods from the denominator. |

## 11. Sources

- Bacon, C. R. (2021). Practical Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement (2nd ed.). Wiley.

## 12. OpenFactsheet convention

Denominator includes all observations (zeros count as not positive).
